However, the ideals $a_0$ and $a_\infty$ used to construct $x' = x_0 / x_\infty$ are defined in [p8-9]--[p8-16] and [p9-9] via the prime ideal factorizations of $(x)$ and $(x - a_j)$, which vary with each $x$. Thus no single $x'$ exists that satisfies the stated theorem for all $x$.

findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: Let q = 2, \delta_v = 1, |x - a_1|_v = |x - a_2|_v = 1, and |x'|_v = 10. Then |x - a_i|_v > \delta_v / 2 = 1/2 for all i, but the left hand side is \prod_{j=1}^2 |x'/(x - a_j)|_{v+} = 10^2 = 100, which is strictly greater than (2/\delta_v)_+^2 = 2^2 = 4, contradicting the claimed inequality in [p7-10]. Thus, the bound erroneously omits |x'|_v from the numerator of each term in the product. Furthermore, the second inequality in [p7-10] also fails whenever |x' / ((x-a_1)...(x-a_q))|_v < 1 because |y|_{v+} = 1 for any |y|_v <= 1, so the factor cannot simply be multiplied into the upper bound without it being bounded from below by 1 independently of x'. Both steps fail because |x'|_v is omitted from the upper bound on the product of |x'/(x-a_j)|_{v+}. As a result, the desired estimate (17) fails to hold uniformly when |x-a_i|_v > \delta_v/2 and |x'|_v is large, rendering the proof of (17) and Theorem 2.1 flawed as stated at [p7-10]. Thus, the bound (2/\delta_v)_+^q incorrectly omits |x'|_v in the estimate. More directly, the claimed upper bound of \prod_{j=1}^q |x'/(x - a_j)|_{v+} has no dependence on x', which is false whenever |x'|_v > 2/\delta_v. Let x' have |x'|_v > 2/\delta_v, then with |x-a_j|_v = 1 > \delta_v/2, the LHS is |x'|_v^q > (2/\delta_v)^q, contradicting the first inequality in [p7-10]. Thus the bound (2/\delta_v)_+^q fails because it erroneously omits |x'|_v. Specifically: \prod_{j=1}^q |x'/(x - a_j)|_{v+} \le |x'|_{v+}^q (2/\delta_v)_+^q rather than (2/\delta_v)_+^q. And since this would leave a power of |x'|_v^q on the left, it cannot be bounded by |x'/ \prod (x - a_j)|_{v+} which only has a single power of x'. In either case, the stated inequality in [p7-10] is mathematically incorrect. Therefore, [p7-10] is in error as claimed. For our witness, take q = 2, \delta_v = 2, |x - a_1|_v = |x - a_2|_v = 2 > 1 = \delta_v/2, and |x'|_v = 4. Then LHS = \max(1, 4/2)^2 = 4, but (2/\delta_v)_+^q = 1^2 = 1 < 4, showing the inequality fails because x' is omitted from the numerator of the bound in [p7-10]. For the witness, we provide the corrected upper bound: \prod_{j=1}^q |x'/(x - a_j)|_{v+} \le |x'|_{v+}^q (2/\delta_v)_+^q.
